chunks: Ali ibn Hatim from al-Zurari from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sadan ibn Muslim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Abi Mansur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

You say between every two takbirs in the Eid prayers: 'O God, Owner of Majesty and Greatness, Owner of Generosity and Power, Owner of Pardon and Mercy, Owner of Piety and Forgiveness. I ask You on this day which You have made a festival for the Muslims and a treasure and increase for Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as best as You sent blessings upon a servant from Your servants. And send blessings upon Your near angels and Your messengers, and forgive the believing men and believing women, the Muslim men and Muslim women, both the living among them and the dead. O God, I ask You from the best that Your sent messengers asked You, and I seek refuge in You from the evil from which Your sent messengers sought refuge in You.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite between takbirs in Eid prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith prescribes a comprehensive supplication to be recited between the takbirs of Eid prayers, emphasizing the dual themes of divine majesty (*al-Kibriya*) and mercy (*al-Jud*). It uniquely links the celebration of Eid to the Prophet Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt as the ultimate 'treasure' (*dhukhr*) of the occasion, while invoking blessings upon the Prophet, the appointed angels, and all believers, living and dead. This practice reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating specific liturgical invocations with broader theological affirmations of God’s attributes and the intercessory role of the Prophet.
